key_insight: LLM2R reframes 3D part assembly as a single-pass sequence modeling problem with a pretrained decoder-only LLM, using summary tokens to collect global context for all parts.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable way to reconstruct fractured or disassembled shapes with many parts, improving pose prediction speed and robustness for CAD, robotics, and damage-reassembly workflows.
method: Encode each part with Point-BERT + Q-Former into geometric token blocks
Concatenate all part tokens and process them with a LoRA-adapted causal LLM in one forward pass
Append learnable summary tokens so every part can access global assembly context before pose prediction
evidence_signal: The method reports top performance on three PartNet categories, PartNeXt, and Breaking Bad, with especially large gains as part count increases and faster inference on Breaking Bad.
watch_item: Because causal attention is directional, earlier part states cannot directly use later-part context except through the appended summary tokens, so performance may depend on token ordering and summary-token design.
paper_title: LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers
